blocks.overview: This case concerns the assessment of costs following the Applicant's discontinuance of a judicial review against the Respondent, Tataskweyak Cree Nation. The Applicant discontinued the proceeding, and the Respondent sought costs for work done on a motion to strike. The court allowed part of the Respondent's Bill of Costs totaling $1,075.20 payable by the Applicant.

blocks.issue: Are the claims for costs related to Items 5, 13(a), and 15 allowable given the Applicant discontinued the proceeding before the motion hearing?
blocks.court_conclusion: Claims for Items 5, 13(a), and 15 are disallowed as the motion was not abandoned and no court order on costs exists.

positions.text: Claimed 5 units for Item 5, 3 units for Item 13(a), and 5 units for Item 15 related to motion to strike.
Rules 370, 402, 411 apply to abandonment by moving party; here Respondent did not abandon motion, Applicant discontinued proceeding before hearing; no authority to allow these claims.
Costs are discretionary; silence on costs implies no costs awarded; court cannot revisit earlier orders silent on costs.

blocks.issue: What amount of costs is reasonable and necessary for the Respondent's work on the motion to strike the Applicant's judicial review application?
blocks.court_conclusion: Allowing 2 units under Item 27 and 6 units total for assessable services is reasonable, totaling $1,075.20 inclusive of taxes.

positions.text: Performed considerable work preparing motion to strike including affidavit and 13-page Written Representations; claimed costs accordingly.
Some indemnification for work on motion is supported; discretion must be reasonable and equitable; allowed 2 units under Item 27 and 6 units total.
Discretion in costs is fettered by reasonable necessity and limits; costs must be just, expeditious, and least expensive.

propositions.text: Applicant filed a Notice of Discontinuance on April 12, 2022, discontinuing judicial review against Respondents.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant discontinued the judicial review proceeding against the Respondents on April 12, 2022, as stated by the court.

propositions.text: Rules 402 and 412 of Federal Courts Rules govern costs for discontinued proceedings and motions.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Rules 402 and 412 of the Federal Courts Rules govern costs for discontinued proceedings and motions.

propositions.text: In absence of specific court decision, costs assessed per Rule 407 of FCR using Tariff B column III.

paragraphs.summary: The court will assess costs under Rule 407 of the FCR using Tariff B column III absent specific court orders.

propositions.text: Respondent Tataskweyak Cree Nation filed Bill of Costs and covering letter on April 20, 2022, requesting cost assessment.

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent filed a Bill of Costs and covering letter on April 20, 2022, requesting cost assessment.

propositions.text: Tataskweyak Cree Nation will be referred to as Respondent in these Reasons.

paragraphs.summary: The court clarifies Tataskweyak Cree Nation is the Respondent in these Reasons.

propositions.text: Direction issued April 25, 2022, for filing additional documents; no further documents filed except Respondent's Bill of Costs.

paragraphs.summary: The court issued a direction for additional documents, but only the Respondent's Bill of Costs was filed.

propositions.text: Applicant did not file responding documents; Respondent's Bill of Costs is substantially unopposed.
Dahl v Canada states absence of relevant representations leaves bill of costs unopposed; assessment officer must not act as advocate but cannot certify unlawful items.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant did not respond, leaving the Respondent's Bill of Costs unopposed, per Dahl v Canada guidance on assessment officers' roles.

propositions.text: Carlile v Canada states Taxing Officers must balance avoiding unnecessary costs and indemnifying real costs on balance of probabilities.

paragraphs.summary: Carlile v Canada guides that Taxing Officers must balance avoiding unnecessary costs and indemnifying real costs on balance of probabilities.

propositions.text: Despite no Applicant response, court must ensure allowed claims are necessary and reasonable using Dahl and Carlile as guidelines.

paragraphs.summary: The court must ensure allowed costs are necessary and reasonable despite no Applicant response, guided by Dahl and Carlile.

propositions.text: Respondent claimed 17 units for assessable services totaling $3,046.00 inclusive of taxes.

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent claimed 17 units of assessable services totaling $3,046.00 inclusive of taxes.

propositions.text: Items 25 and 26 services are necessary and reasonable; 1 unit allowed for Item 25 and 3 units for Item 26.
Items 5, 13(a), and 15 claims have issues requiring detailed assessment.

paragraphs.summary: The court allows Items 25 and 26 as necessary and reasonable but finds issues with Items 5, 13(a), and 15 requiring further assessment.

propositions.text: Respondent claimed 5 units for Item 5, 3 units for Item 13(a), and 5 units for Item 15 related to motion to strike filed April 8, 2022.

paragraphs.summary: The Respondent claimed units for Items 5, 13(a), and 15 related to the motion to strike filed April 8, 2022.

propositions.text: Items 5, 13(a), and 15 relate to Respondent's motion to strike Applicant's judicial review application.
Rule 402 FCR entitles party against whom action discontinued to costs unless otherwise ordered or agreed.

paragraphs.summary: Items 5, 13(a), and 15 relate to Respondent's motion to strike; Rule 402 FCR entitles costs to party against whom action discontinued unless ordered otherwise.

propositions.text: Rule 411 FCR allows costs for abandoned motions assessed on filing of notice of motion or abandonment.

paragraphs.summary: Rule 411 FCR allows costs for abandoned motions assessed on filing of notice of motion or abandonment.

propositions.text: Rule 370 FCR defines abandonment of motion by serving notice or failure to appear as deemed abandonment.

paragraphs.summary: Rule 370 FCR defines abandonment of motion by notice or failure to appear as deemed abandonment.

propositions.text: Rules 370, 402, 411 apply to abandonment by moving party; here Respondent did not abandon motion, Applicant discontinued proceeding before hearing.
Tursunbayev v Canada states court cannot revisit earlier orders silent on costs.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds abandonment rules apply to moving party; Respondent did not abandon motion; Applicant discontinued proceeding; Tursunbayev says court cannot revisit silent cost orders.

propositions.text: Canada v Uzoni states costs are discretionary; silence on costs implies no costs awarded; supported by Mark M. Orkin and Kibale v Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Canada v Uzoni and authorities hold that silence on costs implies no costs awarded as costs are discretionary.

propositions.text: Assessment Officer lacks authority to allow Items 5, 13(a), 15 claims as motion not abandoned and no court costs order exists.
Items 13 and 15 do not apply to motions but to trials and hearings; only Item 5 claim was accurate but still disallowed.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds it lacks authority to allow Items 5, 13(a), and 15 claims; Items 13 and 15 do not apply to motions; Item 5 claim disallowed.

propositions.text: Jurisprudence does not guide motions not disposed or abandoned when underlying proceeding discontinued.
Possible indemnification for preparation and filing of motion not disposed or abandoned depends on file facts.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes lack of guidance for motions not disposed or abandoned when proceeding discontinued; indemnification may depend on facts.

propositions.text: Respondent filed Motion Record April 8, 2022; Applicant did not respond and discontinued proceeding April 12, 2022.
Respondent performed considerable work preparing motion to strike, including affidavit and 13-page Written Representations.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Respondent filed Motion Record April 8; Applicant discontinued April 12; Respondent did considerable work preparing motion and representations.

propositions.text: Some indemnification for work by Respondent on motion to strike Applicant's judicial review application is supported
Mitchell v Canada states discretion in costs is fettered by reasonable necessity and limits of award
Discretion in costs should be part of a reasoned process to achieve equitable results for both sides

paragraphs.summary: The court finds some indemnification for Respondent's work on motion to strike is supported, citing Mitchell v Canada on costs discretion.

propositions.text: Rule 3 of the FCR requires just, expeditious, and least expensive determination of proceedings

paragraphs.summary: Rule 3 of the FCR mandates just, expeditious, and least expensive determination of proceedings.

propositions.text: Assessing Respondent's claim under Item 27 is acceptable and allows positive application of costs provisions
Zero dollars at taxation would be absurd
Considered factors under Rule 400(3) including result, work amount, conduct, and other relevant matters
Allowing 2 units under Item 27 for Respondent's work on motion to strike Applicant's judicial review application is reasonable

paragraphs.summary: The court finds assessing Respondent's claim under Item 27 reasonable, considering Rule 400(3) factors and avoiding zero costs.

propositions.text: 6 units allowed for Respondent's assessable services totaling $1,075.20 inclusive of taxes

paragraphs.summary: The court finds 6 units allowed for Respondent's services totaling $1,075.20 inclusive of taxes.

propositions.text: Respondent did not submit any claims for disbursements

paragraphs.summary: The court notes Respondent did not submit any disbursement claims.

propositions.text: Respondent Tataskweyak Cree Nation's Bill of Costs allowed in total $1,075.20 payable by Applicant
Certificate of Assessment will be issued

paragraphs.summary: The court orders Respondent's Bill of Costs allowed at $1,075.20 payable by Applicant and issues Certificate of Assessment.
